ordered_parameters: P : IntegralPointData X with finite S
positive divisor weights p_i and positive c
r >= 4, irreducible distinct boundary components, no common point of three
p_i * p_j * (D_i . D_j) = c for every distinct pair

source_pinpoint.citation: Pietro Corvaja and Umberto Zannier, On integral points on surfaces, Annals of Mathematics 160 (2004), 705-726, DOI 10.4007/annals.2004.160.705
source_pinpoint.locator: Theorem 1, pages 706-707; arXiv math/0206100 source lines 109-133

source_resolution: The supplied Corvaja/Evertse and curves metadata is erroneous. The 2004 source matching its integral-point degeneracy gloss is Corvaja--Zannier's surface Theorem 1; Evertse appears only as a cited quantitative Subspace-Theorem input on page 708.
root_conclusion: There exists a proper curve on X containing every S-integral k-point in X(k).
encoding_boundary: Scheme and number-field finite-place objects use mathlib. Divisors, intersection numbers, rational/integral points, and curves are source-faithful typed interfaces because pinned mathlib lacks the required combined surface intersection and S-integral-point API. No theorem hypothesis or conclusion is replaced by an opaque proposition.

mutation_review.removed_hypothesis: Removing r >= 4 is not source-equivalent; Example 1.1 demonstrates density without the necessary boundary conditions.
mutation_review.changed_domain: Replacing the geometrically irreducible nonsingular projective surface by an arbitrary scheme is not source-equivalent.
mutation_review.changed_binder_scope: Allowing weights or c to depend on the divisor pair changes the single global family required by the source.
mutation_review.boundary_case: Zero weights or c, fewer than four divisors, or three components sharing a point are excluded explicitly.

status_boundary: The exact source-pinpointed Theorem 1 target elaborates with pinned imports and a checked exact-type fixture. No proof, anchor audit, H0/source-errata closure, validation, release, or master acceptance is claimed.
